title: Transactional outbox between shipping and tracking services
name: Shipment event outbox

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps the shipping database and the tracking service consistent? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The publisher sends event 7 successfully, then the send of event 8 times out. What is the state after publishPending returns?
choices: Events 7 and 8 are both unpublished because the whole transaction is rolled back
Event 7 is marked published and committed, event 8 stays unpublished and is retried on the next poll, and no later event is sent before it
Event 7 is marked published, and the loop skips event 8 and continues with event 9
Event 8 is marked published anyway because the broker may have received it

questions.prompt: The publisher service runs as three replicas. What does the PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the polling query achieve?
choices: Replicas serialize on the batch: one holds the rows while sending, and the others wait and then see them published
It makes Kafka deliver every event exactly once to the tracking service
Each replica locks a different subset of rows and publishes in parallel
It prevents ShipmentService from inserting new outbox rows while a batch is being published

questions.prompt: The tracking service applies an event, then the transaction fails on commit, and Kafka redelivers the record. What happens on redelivery?
choices: insertIfNew returns 0 because the processed marker was committed first, so the update is skipped and lost
The listener fails permanently because the processed_event primary key already exists
The marker insert was rolled back with the update, so insertIfNew returns 1 and the event is applied again
The event is applied twice, because the marker is stored outside the transaction
